verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's own docs show typo tolerance is on by default ("even when they misspell... No tuning required"). They also document tuning: per-index typo-tolerance configuration, a minWordSizeForTypos override for when typos are allowed, and a built-in 'typo' ranking rule whose order can be changed. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of typo-tolerance behavior, and fuller documentation of the remaining tunable rules (e.g., disabling typos on specific words or attributes) beyond minWordSizeForTypos.

support.subject: As a developer, searches tolerate typos and misspellings out of the box, with tunable rules for when and how fuzzy matching applies

citations.quote: Typo tolerance helps users find relevant results even when their search queries contain spelling mistakes or typos, for example, typing `phnoe` instead of `phone`.
Help users find what they want instantly, even when they misspell or only remember part of it. No tuning required.
You can override these default settings using the minWordSizeForTypos object.
You can configure the typo tolerance feature for each index
Meilisearch contains seven built-in ranking rules in the following order: ["words", "typo", "proximity", "attributeRank", "sort", "wordPosition", "exactness"]
